In nNOS-transfected human kidney 293 cells, EPR spin-trapping showed the Ca²⁺ ionophore A23187 triggered NO without ·O₂⁻ in controls, whereas L-Arg-free medium produced ·O₂⁻ that rose as cytosolic L-Arg fell while NO declined; L-NAME abolished ·O₂⁻. Nitrotyrosine accumulated in L-Arg-depleted cells, where A23187 was cytotoxic (marked LDH release), largely prevented by superoxide dismutase or L-NAME — indicating peroxynitrite-mediated injury; thus arginine regulation is a therapeutic target. Separately, p53 is activated by DNA damage (IR, radio-mimetic drugs, UV, MMS), hypoxia and nucleotide deprivation; kept low by its short half-life and weak DNA binding, activation raises its levels and DNA binding, inducing cell-cycle arrest, apoptosis or DNA repair via phosphorylation, dephosphorylation and acetylation of p53.
